cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine build HANGS Construction's thirteen-week cash forecast.
It starts from the reconciled bank balance, and checks last week's forecast against the bank.
Next it schedules the payments: this week's supplier batch, every other open bill, and seven payrolls.
Each bill lands in the run on or before its due date.
Then receipts: contract payments count only with a signed contract.
It also adds the approved construction loan draws.
A site with no signed contract stays out.
Then construction costs, loan interest and rent.
The steel order, about $552,000, is due in December.
Now it rolls all thirteen weeks forward.
The lowest week, in early December, ends about $40,000 below the minimum balance.
It offers two ways to fix it.
Week thirteen ends near $1.48 million, with four flags for a person to decide.
All done. The forecast is ready, with the lowest week flagged below the minimum. Nothing was paid, posted or drawn; the controller decides each flag and approves.
Jumping to the results. A person still reviews every item before anything is posted, paid or sent.
